observations.text: SP, due to an unstabilized power setting during the transition to the formation approach as leader, did not maintain the briefed approach airspeed and altitude, with the result of a 25-knot airspeed excursion and a 340-foot altitude deviation, both beyond the code 1 tolerance. The IP directed the pitch and power corrections and flew part of the final segment. The formation approach cannot yet be completed without assistance.

SP, due to inadequate crew coordination between front and rear cockpit, did not keep the briefed wingman position in landing configuration during the formation approach, with the result that lateral separation closed inside the 10-foot minimum reference point and the observance angle opened past 55 degrees. The IP took the aircraft and repositioned the formation before the approach was continued. Repeat instruction on fingertip position references and on cross-talk with the leader is required.

SP, due to a late power reduction while establishing the formation on final as leader, did not hold the briefed approach parameters, with the result of a 300-foot altitude deviation, a 20-knot airspeed excursion and a 10-degree exit heading error, all at the limit of the code 1 tolerance. Both the airspeed and the altitude were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts. No intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to an unshared assessment of the aircraft state between front and rear cockpit, did not report the drift out of the fingertip reference during the formation approach, with the result that lateral separation opened to 20 feet beyond the reference point and vertical separation reached 10 feet above the leader's wing level, at the code 1 limits. The briefed position was regained only after the IP's verbal corrections, with delayed recognition by SP. Plain-language cross-talk on the developing deviation is expected before the next formation recovery.

SP flew the formation approach within the desired standards for the Training Section, holding airspeed within 15 knots and altitude within 250 feet of the briefed approach values. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention; however, three separate power corrections were needed on the final segment. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother throttle control and earlier anticipation of the leader's power changes are expected to improve.

SP executed the formation approach as leader with accuracy and speed and without IP's intervention, holding altitude within 100 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and exit heading within 3 degrees of the briefed values. Configuration changes and radio calls were standard and timely throughout the recovery. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation approach in the wingman position with exceptional precision, keeping lateral and vertical separation with negligible deviations from the fingertip reference and holding the observance angle steady at the 30-degree value in landing configuration. Corrections were anticipated rather than reactive, and no IP prompting was required at any point of the approach. Performance was above the desired level for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
